public_rationale: The claim is about one session with the free version of ChatGPT on or about 4 February 2025. Marcus describes the session as lasting 10 minutes. Under the contract, the claim is supported only if the shared transcript, or an independent check of it, shows two or more state tables that each left out at least one state. The evidence includes neither the transcript nor such a check. A post by Benjamin Todd, available on 9 February 2025, says "GPT-4o misses out a bunch of states" (e1). It does not say how many of Marcus's tables left out states. It also does not say whether Todd looked at Marcus's transcript. A reader comment dated 5 February 2025 says the reader's own GPT-4o run left out states (e2). That was a different session, so it does not show what happened in Marcus's session. The evidence neither confirms nor rules out two or more incomplete tables.
limitations: The shared transcript linked in Marcus's post was not found, so none of his tables could be checked against the list of 50 states.
e1 does not show whether its author checked Marcus's transcript, or how many of Marcus's tables left out states.
e2 describes a different session and cannot show what Marcus's session produced.
